'understanding of him' or 'his' = God's understanding; [completeness] "you will consider that yourself" vs "καὶ σὺ αὐτὸς ἐπιστήσεις": dropped 'also/and' (καί); 'that yourself' obscures 'you yourself' as subject; [modality] "The angels would be those in the heavens" vs "Ἄγγελοι μὲν ἂν εἶεν οἱ ἐν οὐρανοῖς": ἂν εἶεν is potential optative ('would be' as tentative identification), but 'would be' in English suggests hypothetical/unreal; better 'would be' as conjectural identification; [completeness] "they are above the task of bringing messages" vs "ὑπὲρ τὸ διαγγέλλειν ἀνθρώποις οὖσαι": dropped 'to human beings' (ἀνθρώποις); 'bringing messages' alone misses recipients; [negation] "they have their blessedness only in their perpetual steadfastness with God" vs "ἐν δὲ μόνῃ τῇ παρὰ θεῷ βεβαιότητι διηνεκῇ τὸ μακάριον ἔχουσαι": correctly rendered; 'only' properly translates μόνῃ; [agency] "the name indicating that God is seated upon them" vs "ἐνδεικνυμένου τοῦ ὀνόματος τὸ ἐφιδρῦσθαι αὐταῖς τὸν θεόν": genitive absolute 'the name indicating' correct, but 'is seated' for ἐφιδρῦσθαι (perfect infinitive 'to have been seated') loses perfect aspect of established seating; [completeness] "and that they are subject to the divine majesty" vs "τὰς δὲ ὑποκεῖσθαι τῇ θείᾳ καὶ ὑπὲρ κτίσιν μεγαλειότητι": τὰς = 'them' (feminine, referring to thrones), not 'they'; 'they are subject' misses that accusative τάς continues infinitive construction with ἐφιδρῦσθαι, both governed by τὸ; [completeness] "they stand always in this" vs "ἐν τούτῳ δὴ καθεστηκυίας ἀεὶ": καθεστηκυίας is perfect participle 'having been established/standing,' but 'they stand' misses that this continues accusative construction (τὰς...καθεστηκυίας), still describing thrones; [completeness] "and have their fixed and stable state" vs "καὶ τὸ στάσιμον καὶ πεπηγὸς ἐχούσας": ἐχούσας accusative continues construction; 'have their...state' adds 'state' not in Greek, which has 'the fixed and stable' as direct object of 'having'; [completeness] "in receiving the divine glory" vs "ἐν τῇ τῆς θείας δόξης ὑποδοχῇ": 'receiving' for ὑποδοχῇ ('reception') is acceptable; but 'the reception' is nominal, not verbal; [scripture] "(Psalm 148:3-4)" vs "312 Ps 148,3.4": apparatus shows 3.4 (LXX 148:3-4), but English brackets as 148:3-4; however source has *** φέγγη *** indicating lacuna, and English notes '[The text is damaged here: …]' which is editorial addition; [completeness] "the lights [that shine] in heaven" vs "φέγγη *** οὐρανῷ": editorial '[that shine]' added; φέγγη alone is 'lights' or 'brightnesses'; [completeness] "illuminating the heaven itself, the highest one" vs "φωτίζοντα αὐτόν τε τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸν ἀνωτάτω": αὐτόν τε = 'itself both' or 'both itself'; 'the heaven itself' misses τε 'both/and' linking to next item; [completeness] "and also the water above this" vs "καὶ δὴ τού του δὲ ἀνώτερον ὕδωρ": τούτου δὲ ἀνώτερον = 'above this,' but 'this' refers to firmament; 'also' for δή is weak; καὶ δὴ = 'and indeed'; [modality] "he exhorts to praise God" vs "ὑμνεῖν τὸν θεὸν παρακελεύεται": παρακελεύεται takes dative of person + infinitive; subject is David/psalmist; 'he exhorts' correct but missing object 'them' (the lights/water) | part 2/2: [source_identity] "how worthy of all praise their Maker is" vs "τὸ πανύμνητον ἐμφανίζοντα τοῦ δημιουργήσαντος": "Maker" obscures δημιουργήσαντος (one who crafted/designed); "worthy of all praise" is interpretive expansion of πανύμνητον (all-praiseworthy); [agency] "he points to those from every nation" vs "ὑποδείκνυσι": Subject is unclear: ὑποδείκνυσι lacks explicit subject, but context suggests the psalmist/scripture, not "he" as if a person; [modality] "he shows that its following comes after the nations" vs "ἐπακολούθησιν αὐτοῦ δηλοῖ τὴν μετὰ τὰ ἔθνη": Ambiguous whether ἐπακολούθησιν is "following" (act of following) or "those who follow"; "its following" is unclear; [scripture] "Psalm 4:9 (4:8)" vs "Ἐν εἰρήνῃ [ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ] κοιμηθήσομαι καὶ ὑπνώσω": Citation should be Psalm 4:8 (4:9 Hebrew) per LXX numbering, but the verse quoted is actually Psalm 4:9 in LXX (4:8 Hebrew); the bracketed [ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ] is present in some LXX manuscripts
